title: healingMul is an inert lever: tuned, swept and exported but never read by the engine
body:
## Summary
TuningOverrides.healingMul is offered as a sweep lever, a goal-seek lever and a UE5 export field, but src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts never reads it, so every healingMul setting produces the same fight.

## Description
src/types/combat-simulator.ts:89 declares healingMul (0.5-2.0); src/lib/combat/definitions.ts:347 defaults it; src/lib/combat/sweep-tuning.ts:58 sweeps it as 'Healing'; src/lib/combat/goal-seek.ts:18 lists it as a goal-seek lever; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/ue5-export.ts:53 writes it to C++. grep of simulation-engine.ts for 'healing' returns 0 lines. A sweep over it reports zero sensitivity and goal-seek can 'move' it to no effect. The bakeoff backlog card asking to add a healingMul slider to TUNING_SLIDERS was rejected this round for this reason: it would add an inert control. Fixed means either the engine applies healingMul where player HP is restored, or the lever is removed from sweep/goal-seek until it does.

## Flow
- grep -n healing src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts -> 0 lines
- run a seeded simulation with healingMul 0.5 and 2.0 -> identical summaries (prediction)
- fix: apply healingMul where player HP is restored, or drop it from the sweep / goal-seek levers

## Expected impact
Designers stop reading a flat sensitivity line as 'healing does not matter'. Risk: applying it changes seeded outputs of runs with healing sources; pinned engine tests may need re-pinning.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a declared tuning lever actually moves the simulation
Before: engine reads of healingMul: 0 (grep); sites that offer it as a lever or export: 3
After: engine reads >= 1 and a seeded A/B at 0.5 vs 2.0 shows a different HP-left figure, or the 3 offering sites drop it
Method: probe - grep over the engine; the seeded A/B run is the instrument, not built because the engine and sweep files are outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts: 0 matches for 'healing'
src/lib/combat/sweep-tuning.ts:58  { lever: 'healingMul', label: 'Healing', range: [0.5, 2] }
src/lib/combat/goal-seek.ts:18 ... | 'healingMul'
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/ue5-export.ts:53 HealingMul
instrument: vitest: seeded simulate() with a healing source at healingMul 0.5 vs 2.0 must differ in avgPlayerHealthRemaining; red today

title: Run accepts an empty ability loadout and simulates a player who never acts
body:
## Summary
The Run gate (canRun) checks tuning, config and gear but not abilities, so after 'Clear' the simulator runs N fights in which the player never attacks.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/index.tsx:121 canRun = !!tuning && !!defaultConfig && !!gear; src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/ScenarioBuilder.tsx:112 'Clear' empties the loadout. With playerAbilities [] the engine's choosePlayerAbility (src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts:496-509) always returns null, so every fight is a loss or timeout and the report reads as a balance verdict ('Brutal') rather than a configuration error. Fixed: canRun also requires playerAbils.length > 0 and the button says why.

## Flow
- click Clear in Abilities
- click Run 1000 Fights
- report shows a brutal encounter that is really an empty loadout

## Expected impact
Designers no longer read a misconfiguration as a balance result. Risk: none beyond a disabled button.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a misconfigured run is refused, not reported as a verdict
Before: runs accepted with 0 abilities: allowed (canRun ignores abilities)
After: refused with a stated reason
Method: simulation - walked the gate and the engine's choosePlayerAbility; a seeded engine run on [] was not taken
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: Clear abilities -> Run button disabled (red today); plus a seeded engine run on [] to record what the report says

title: Threat-row 'top threat' cuts restate the engine's nerf thresholds inline
body:
## Summary
ThreatRow's isTopThreat uses killShare >= 0.4 || damageShare >= 0.3, the same cuts suggestAbilityNerf uses for 'Headline killer' and 'Spammed source', as independent literals in two files.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/ThreatBreakdownPanel.tsx (ThreatRow) `killShare >= 0.4 || damageShare >= 0.3`; src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts suggestAbilityNerf `killShare >= 0.4` and `damageShare >= 0.3`. Tuning one side leaves a row painted red with no headline nerf, or the reverse. Same class as the 'Within tolerance.' sentinel fixed this round (23b4702c). Fixed: export the cuts from the engine and read them on both sides.

## Flow
- export const THREAT_CUTS = { headlineKill: 0.4, spammedDamage: 0.3 } from the engine
- use it in suggestAbilityNerf and ThreatRow
- source-guard test like combat-sim-nerf-sentinel.test.ts

## Expected impact
Prevents silent drift between the highlight and the suggestion. Risk: negligible.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition per threshold
Before: threshold literal pairs restated across 2 files: 2
After: 0 restated; 1 definition each
Method: probe - read both sites; routed B because the definition belongs in the engine and the view-side gain alone is small
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
ThreatBreakdownPanel.tsx ThreatRow: const isTopThreat = killShare >= 0.4 || damageShare >= 0.3;
simulation-engine.ts suggestAbilityNerf: if (killShare >= 0.4) ... if (damageShare >= 0.3 && ...)
instrument: source-scan test counting the two literals across both files (2 -> 0)

title: ABILITY_GROUPS is a hand list with no exhaustiveness gate over the ability type union
body:
## Summary
The ability picker renders only types listed in ABILITY_GROUPS; a new CombatAbility type would silently vanish from the picker with no gate failing.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/constants.ts:44-50 lists 5 types; src/types/combat-simulator.ts:24 union has 5 today (complete). src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/ScenarioBuilder.tsx:123 iterates ABILITY_GROUPS only, so an ability whose type is missing is never rendered while selectedCount (ScenarioBuilder.tsx:44) still counts it. Fixed: key labels by Record<CombatAbility['type'], string> so tsc rejects a missing type.

## Flow
- add a 6th member to CombatAbility['type']
- tsc stays green today; abilities of that type disappear from the picker
- after: tsc fails on the missing Record key

## Expected impact
Future-proofs the picker. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - drift between the type union and the picker is caught by a gate
Before: gates that fail when a type is added without a group: 0
After: 1 (tsc)
Method: simulation - walked adding a type; seeding the union was not done because types/combat-simulator.ts is shared outside this context
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: seed a 6th union member in a scratch worktree and confirm tsc goes red after the Record change

title: Scenario defaults are literal catalog ids; a catalog without them silently simulates zero enemies
body:
## Summary
The initial loadout, initial enemy group and '+ Add enemy group' hardcode ids ('melee-grunt', 'ga-*', 'starter'); if the catalog API omits one, the select displays another archetype while the run submits the missing id, which the engine skips.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/index.tsx:82-87 literal ability/enemy ids; src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/ScenarioBuilder.tsx:231 new group archetypeId 'melee-grunt'. All exist in src/lib/combat/definitions.ts today (lines 46,58,70,82,121,139,311). But the engine does `if (!archetype) continue;` (src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts:298), so a stale id yields an encounter with fewer or zero enemies and no error. Fixed: derive defaults from the loaded catalog.

## Flow
- catalog returns archetypes without melee-grunt
- select shows the first archetype (controlled value has no matching option)
- Run submits melee-grunt; engine skips it; fights have 0 enemies

## Expected impact
A catalog change cannot silently produce an empty encounter. Risk: the default loadout follows catalog order.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - stale default ids cannot reach the engine
Before: default kinds validated against the loaded catalog: 0 of 3
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - walked the controlled-select mismatch and the engine skip; which archetype becomes the default is a small product choice
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: store enemies without melee-grunt -> every submitted archetypeId exists in the catalog (red today)

title: Four Scenario labels are orphaned from their controls
body:
## Summary
ScenarioBuilder renders <label> elements for Player Level, Iterations, Abilities and Enemies with no htmlFor, so clicking the label focuses nothing; only Gear is wired.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CombatSimulatorView/ScenarioBuilder.tsx:57,82,100,173 <label> without htmlFor; NumberField supports an id prop (src/components/ui/NumberField.tsx:22) so the two numeric fields can be wired with useId like Gear (ScenarioBuilder.tsx:69). Abilities/Enemies are group captions, better as a heading or fieldset legend. Screen readers already get aria-label on the inputs, so the gain is pointer label activation and correct semantics.

## Flow
- click 'Player Level' text
- focus does not move to the field

## Expected impact
Small semantic and pointer gain. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - labels activate their controls
Before: labels wired to a control: 1 of 5
After: 5 of 5 (2 via htmlFor, 2 as group captions)
Method: simulation - DOM read of the five labels; not built this round for budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
ScenarioBuilder.tsx:57 <label ...>Player Level</label>
:82 Iterations
:100 Abilities
:173 Enemies
:69 htmlFor={gearSelectId} (the one wired)
instrument: component test: getByLabelText('Player Level') resolves to the input (throws today)
